editorial:
After her son starts acting strange and comes home with a bruised face, a single mother storms into his school demanding answers. What starts as a simple complaint quickly spirals into something much bigger, as teachers, parents, and kids all tell different versions of the same event. You never quite know who to trust, and that uncertainty keeps you glued to the screen. The story unfolds in layers, showing the same moments from different angles, which makes you rethink everything you thought you knew. It is a quiet but powerful film that pulls you in with its mystery and emotional weight.

The acting is excellent across the board, especially from the young leads who carry the emotional heart of the story. The pacing is slow and deliberate, so if you want fast action, this might not be for you. But if you enjoy thoughtful dramas that reward patience, you will find a lot to love here. The cinematography is beautiful and the score adds a gentle touch without being overbearing.
endingExplained: In the final act, you learn that the two boys at the center of the story are actually close friends, not enemies. The school incident was a misunderstanding fueled by adults jumping to conclusions. The twist reveals that one boy has been struggling with his identity and the other has been quietly supporting him. In the last scenes, the boys run away together during a storm, and the film ends on a hopeful, open note as they find shelter and smile at each other, suggesting their bond will survive the chaos around them.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves layered dramas with strong performances and a mystery that unfolds slowly.
